assertions.name: y_1cubed_vanishes_under_convention_D
assertions.source: y_(3) + 2 y_(2,1) = 1 to 0.0, and the three block dimensions are 1, 2, 1 -- so y_(1^3) = 0 EXACTLY. This is the two-row truncation that defines convention D (D => vanish is threeRow_eq_zero_of_jones_ocneanu; the converse is markovWeights_eq_jones_of_threeRow_eq_zero + hfaith), not a numerical accident of the pin. It is why reading 3 cannot see the alternating block at all

assertions.name: chi21_of_the_identity_is_the_block_dimension
assertions.source: chi_(2,1)(1) = 2.0, block dimension 2 -- the subtraction extraction is calibrated before any verdict is read off it

assertions.name: the_3_block_can_never_bind_on_this_alphabet
assertions.source: every corpus letter has chi_(3) > 0 (0.900918283956 at worst), and chi_(3) is multiplicative, so chi_(3)(w) > 0 for EVERY word. The whole content of reading 3 on this alphabet is chi_(2,1) >= 0 -- reproduced here independently of the sibling probe that first reported it

assertions.name: reading3_does_not_constrain_the_crossing_budget
assertions.source: every dressing count k = 0..3 has admissible configurations for BOTH nucleons, so reading 3 selects no gluon count. The parity constraint of #7336 (gluon dressing must be ODD) has no force under the live reading -- it is a reading-1 statement

assertions.name: reading3_admits_ODD_length_words_in_quantity
assertions.source: length 9 (4/8) and length 11 (149/288) are both admissible for the proton -- directly contradicting the consequence I drew from the parity theorem, which excluded every odd length. The THEOREM is fine; it is about the block reading 3 ignores

assertions.name: reading3_leaves_exactly_one_survivor_in_the_quark_family
assertions.source: survivors = [(2, 'sigma')], chi_(2,1) = 0.0574586606222. The sibling probe reports the family as entirely rejected; it checks all(is_psd(M)) over EVERY block, which is reading 1. Under the live reading the family is not empty -- so qou-99qc's 'what replaces the element' item has a candidate the reading-1 measurement hid

assertions.name: both_census_assignments_stay_excluded_under_reading3
assertions.source: p (0, 'sigma') chi_(2,1) = -0.280593350903, n (2, 'inv') chi_(2,1) = -0.371956324741 -- both negative, and y_(2,1) = 0.24729789 > 0, so the (2,1) failure BINDS. The element rejection stands on (2,1) alone; nothing downstream of it moves and the L2 rows stay un-re-scored

assertions.name: reading1_would_annihilate_every_corpus_nucleon_model
assertions.source: all 3 nucleon constructions in the tree are ODD, so under reading 1 -- where the parity theorem does apply -- every one of them is excluded on LENGTH, whatever its dressing. A survivor would need an even-length model or a letter with shift d >= 4.309370498, against the alphabet's max of 0. That is a fact about reading 1's viability for this corpus, and it is the parity work's real contribution

description: CORRECTS my own merged work (#7319/#7325/#7336). The crossing-budget length-parity exclusion is a READING-1 theorem; the owner selected reading 3 (Frobenius positivity on blocks with y_lambda > 0) on 2026-09-12, and the 2026-09-13 (B) answer moved the LETTER scope, not the reading. Under convention D y_(1^3) = 0, so reading 3 does not constrain the alternating block where the parity theorem lives. Measured: reading 3 admits every dressing count k = 0..3 for both nucleons, including the odd lengths 9 and 11 -- the budget is not decided by this criterion. Two further corrections: the one-letter quark family is NOT empty under reading 3 (1 of 6 survives, (slot 2, sigma), chi_(2,1) = +0.0574586606), and the element rejection that does stand rests on (2,1) ALONE, not on (1,1,1). The parity theorem survives as a statement about the parked reading 1, where it is annihilating: all three corpus nucleon models are odd.
